competitors.name: mean_reversion
competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: You
competitors.rules: Your real Robinhood account, rebased to the shared origin so it's comparable. Performance only — holdings and trades are deliberately not published.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

regime.label: Event-heavy October with policy risk ahead
regime.note: The Federal Reserve calendar places the next FOMC meeting on October 27-28. Low confidence and 64% cash reflect policy-event risk, extended screen leaders, and the analyst book's persistent negative alpha.

analyst.thesis: Hold the September 29 event-driven reset through the October 9 settled session. VRTX and NEM remain pre-event positions rather than tape-following trades: Vertex reports Q3 on November 2 and has the November 30 povetacicept PDUFA, while Newmont reports Q3 after the October 22 close. The randomized whole-universe screen is still crowded: MRNA gained 56.28% over 20 sessions, SHOP 32.66%, CRWD 33.04%, DDOG 32.57%, and PLTR 25.01%; several leaders are overbought or trade at premium or negative earnings multiples. Robinhood fundamentals show VRTX at 29.675655x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.880103x, while the paper book trails SPY by 19.8 points with a -3.58 Sharpe. No new momentum exposure is justified. Retain 64% cash and unchanged low confidence. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists its next two-day FOMC meeting for October 27-28, 2026.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; RAINIER showed a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and a 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001).
Vertex says it will report Q3 2026 results on November 2 after market close and host its call at 4:30 p.m. ET.
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 12 data shows VRTX at 29.675655x P/E, $129.6623 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 12 data shows NEM at 14.880103x P/E, $124.1776 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target.
At the October 9 settled close, VRTX was $510.08 and NEM was $117.84; VRTX is 2.4% below the paper entry and NEM is 7.6% below the paper entry.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
NEM remains 7.6% below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 64% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The portfolio has produced -19.8 points of all-time alpha with a -3.58 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; Vertex reported a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and 49.8% versus placebo (P<0.0001). Vertex also confirmed Q3 results for November 2. The October 9 close was $510.08; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 29.675655/6.382270, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Approval can establish Vertex's nephrology franchise faster than the market credits, but the binary outcome and negative alpha cap the anchor at 20%. [DATA] Buy limit $515.18, about 1% above the settled close.
rationale.NEM: [DATA] Newmont confirmed Q3 results after the October 22 close; Robinhood's earnings calendar shows a $1.93 EPS estimate. The October 9 close was $117.84; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 14.880103/3.540920, Q2 revenue of $6.118 billion, Q2 net income of $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Stable production and costs could produce a favorable result versus the $1.93 consensus, but the negative mark since entry and commodity risk cap the position at 16%. [DATA] Buy limit $119.02, about 1% above the settled close.

reflection.looking_back: The marked book is down 16.2% versus SPY up 3.6%, or -19.8 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.58 annualized 40-session Sharpe. The latest tick was approximately flat on alpha: the book fell 0.3% while SPY fell 0.2%; VRTX is 2.4% below entry and NEM is 7.6% below entry.
worked: VRTX and NEM recovered versus their October 7 marks while retaining company-confirmed future checkpoints, so both theses remain falsifiable.
The 64% cash buffer avoided adding to a screen led by MRNA at +56.28% over 20 sessions, PLTR at +25.01%, SHOP at +32.66%, and DDOG at +32.57%, with several leaders already overbought.
missed: The latest session still failed to add alpha, and all-time alpha remains -19.8 points.
NEM remains the larger detractor at 7.6% below entry, so the October 22 earnings event must validate rather than merely extend the thesis.
reflection.adjustment: Keep confidence at 0.32, hold VRTX at 20% and NEM at 16%, retain 64% cash, and refuse to chase extended software, semiconductor, or biotech leaders before the October catalysts.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 148 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-10-09, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
